finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: attacker-supplied Base64 data is passed to Marshal.load, allowing arbitrary object instantiation and remote code execution via Ruby gadget chains.
finding.source: POST /restore form parameter `state` (params[:state]), fully attacker-controlled, no authentication

trace.note: params[:state] Base64-decoded and passed directly to Marshal.load
result inspected and returned (also triggers inspect on attacker objects)

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, no signature/HMAC on payload, no class allowlist, no safe alternative (JSON) used; no before filters or middleware in app.rb; Sinatra's protection (Rack::Protection) does not prevent this.

verdict.reason: app.rb:5-6 defines an unauthenticated POST /restore that passes Base64-decoded params[:state] straight into Marshal.load, with no auth, signature, allowlist or filter anywhere in the single-file app (app.rb:7 then calls inspect on the result as described).
